Scientists Just Sequenced DNA From the Dead Sea Scrolls — What They Found Shocked Everyone

In 1947, a Bedouin shepherd boy threw a rock into a cave near the Dead Sea, heard something crack inside, and climbed inside to find ancient clay jars holding leather scrolls wrapped in linen. Those scrolls turned out to be the oldest known biblical manuscripts dating back over 2,000 years. They would become the most fought over religious discovery in human history. For 70 years, the greatest scholarly minds on earth studied them and still could not answer the most disturbing questions hiding inside them. Why did the same cave hold multiple completely different versions of the same sacred book? Then in 2020, scientists sequenced ancient DNA extracted directly from the animal skins the scrolls were written on. What they found did not just surprise the academic world. It tore apart everything scholars thought they knew about the Bible, where it actually came from, and how it became what it is today.

snippet.title: D-Day: 100 Days For Freedom
snippet.description:
For the 82nd anniversary of the D-Day Landings, this documentary brings back to life the 100 days it took for the Allies to liberate Normandy, to break through the German line and to pave the way towards victory. 100 critical days, both heroic and tragic, that made history.

“The free men of the world are marching together to Victory!” These are the words of Commander Eisenhower to the Allied troops on June 6, 1944. A few hours later, they were around 150,000 to land on the Normandy coast. Operation “Overlord” was launched: one of the largest military operations of the 20th century. D-Day: 100 Days for Freedom propels us into the 100 sensational days that followed, while reviving the experiences of soldiers on both sides.

 Broadcast in prime time, this film event retraces day by day – from D-Day up to the Liberation of Paris – this key moment of the Second World War, through a series of moving testimonies and spectacular colorized archives, both collective and intimate.
